title: D4a: the distinguish verb, and the citation-versus-legislation ratio it makes measurable
description: Operator ruled YES on D4 (2026-08-17). Add a distinguish verb to precedent.py that disposes of a novel case by citing the nearest decided record plus the material difference, emitted as a signed act via attest.py. Then report the ratio of novel cases disposed by citation versus by legislation. That ratio is the differentiator and nobody else can report it because nobody else has the denominator. Two cautions from the existing layer: PR-022 clause 3 says the event types are exactly six, so check whether a new event type is even available before emitting one; and the ratio needs a defined denominator before it is published, or it becomes another figure with no falsifier. If the denominator cannot be defined honestly, ship the verb and report NO DENOMINATOR RATIFIED rather than inventing one.

notes.note:
HANDOFF -> verifier: T-402 (D4a) DONE by coordinator-opus, handing to a DISTINCT verifier. Sections 2 and 4 are
where the substance is: the task's premise was partly wrong, and the ratio it asked for
cannot be reported as specified.

1. THE GAP THIS ACTUALLY FILLS, WHICH IS NOT THE ONE THE TASK TITLE NAMES

`distinguishes` ALREADY EXISTED as a relation type on `publish`, and has since T-353. So the
layer could already distinguish. The problem is that it could only do so BY PUBLISHING A
RECORD: a permanent, immutable tier-N record under SDR-01, needing its own confirmation under
PR-015. Every novel case therefore cost an act of LEGISLATION.

The new verb disposes of a case by CITATION: it names the nearest decided record and the
material difference, signs that as an act, and CREATES NO RECORD. The registry does not grow.
That is what makes the two paths countable against each other, which is the whole of D4a.

Verify the claim that this was the real gap. If `publish --distinguishes` was already
adequate, this verb is redundant and should be said so.

2. THE CHEAP PATH MUST NOT BE THE LAX PATH, AND THIS IS THE MAIN DESIGN RISK

If distinguishing were easier to do BADLY than legislating, the ratio would measure
corner-cutting and would look better the worse the work got. So every refusal `publish`
applies to a `distinguishes` relation is applied here as well:
  - the target must be in the registry;
  - the target must be `active` (distinguishing from dead law disposes of nothing);
  - the target's scope_conditions must be non-empty (nothing for the facts to fall outside of);
  - the material difference must be non-empty (SDR-17.7).

PLUS ONE STRICTER RULE, and its justification is the thing to attack: a material difference
under 12 words is refused. Grounds: a published record carries a ratio, scope conditions and
confirmation behind it, whereas a distinguish act carries NOTHING but that sentence. It is the
only record of the reasoning, so it must be reviewable alone. TWELVE IS A NUMBER THIS MODULE
CHOSE AND NO RECORD RATIFIED. If a verifier thinks a word count is the wrong instrument, that
is a fair hit -- but say what replaces it, because "no floor at all" is the option that makes
the cheap path the lax path.

All refusals live in one function, `_distinguish_refusals`, so a test enumerates them directly
rather than trusting the CLI path to cover each.

3. THE CAUTION IN THE TASK ABOUT EVENT TYPES WAS BASED ON A CONFLATION

T-402 warned that PR-022 clause 3 fixes the event types at exactly six, so check before
emitting a new one. CHECKED, and the six are REPUTATION event types: rule authorship,
load-bearing citations received, consolidations achieved, proper overrulings issued and
sustained, verification verdicts upheld, adjudications not reversed. They are credit-earning
categories, not log kinds.

DECISIVE EVIDENCE, and it is a test rather than an argument: the live event log already
carries more than six kinds, so if clause 3 governed log kinds this harness would already be
in violation. It is not. `case_distinguished` is emitted. Two tests pin the reasoning, and one
of them fails if a future edit makes clause 3 name log kinds -- at which point the caution
becomes real again.

4. THE RATIO CANNOT BE REPORTED AS SPECIFIED, AND THE OUTPUT SAYS SO

D4 asked for the ratio of NOVEL CASES disposed by citation versus by legislation, and called
it the differentiator because nobody else has the denominator. The honest finding is that
THIS HARNESS DOES NOT HAVE IT EITHER YET.

`disposition-ratio` reports the share of DISPOSITIONS MADE. That is a different denominator
from CASES ARISING. There is no register of cases PRESENTED, so a case that was raised and
never disposed of -- abandoned, forgotten, routed around, or silently answered in prose
without either verb -- is invisible. The numerator split is real and worth watching; the ratio
D4 named is not yet computable.

The output prints NO DENOMINATOR RATIFIED and NO THRESHOLD RATIFIED, following currency.py's
precedent, and it names the SPECIFIC WRONG FIX so nobody reaches for it: building the case
register by inferring cases retroactively from dispositions would make the denominator a
function of the numerator and the ratio would read 1.0 forever. A test asserts that sentence
is present, because it is the sentence most likely to be edited out by someone who wants a
clean number.

VERIFIER: decide whether a case register should be filed as a task. The coordinator did not
file one, on the grounds that it is a design question about what counts as a case in this
harness and not a mechanical gap. Disagree if you think that is a dodge.

5. LIVE FIGURE, WHICH IS THE HONEST STARTING POINT

  dispuestos por cita        0 crudos / 0 distintos
  dispuestos por legislacion 58 crudos / 58 distintos
  cuota de la cita           0.0%

Every case this layer has ever disposed of, it disposed of by legislating. That is the
baseline the ratio exists to move, and it should be quoted as 0 percent OF DISPOSITIONS, never
as 0 percent of cases.

6. A BUG THIS INTRODUCED AND THEN FIXED, WORTH KNOWING

`precedent.py --root` is the PRECEDENTS directory (SDR-13). `attest.py --root` is the HARNESS
root, where acts/, warrants/ and trust/ live. The first implementation handed the precedents
directory to attest, which found no warrants there and refused every name as unable to sign.
Now there is `harness_root_for_acts`, defaulting to the precedents directory's parent, with a
`--harness-root` override and an explicit REFUSAL when neither resolves to something carrying
a trust anchor. Refused rather than guessed, because a wrong root surfaces as "that name can
sign nothing", which points at entirely the wrong problem. Reproduced live: passing
`--root .harness` now gets the correct diagnosis.

7. EVIDENCE, REPLAYABLE

  python3 -m pytest .harness/tests/ -q                              -> 612 passed, 4 skipped
  python3 -m pytest .harness/tests/test_precedent_distinguish.py -q  -> 23 passed
  python3 .harness/bin/precedent.py disposition-ratio               -> the figures in 5
  python3 .harness/bin/precedent.py distinguish ... --root .harness -> the refusal in 6

FIVE NEGATIVE CONTROLS, each in a COPY of .harness, never the live tree:
  A the verb also writes a record   -> 3 fail (incl. the byte-for-byte registry check)
  B the 12-word floor removed       -> 3 fail
  C the target-scope rule removed   -> 2 fail
  D 0/0 prints as 0.0 not None      -> 1 fail
  E dead law counts as legislation  -> 2 fail

The registry check compares BYTES, not a file count, because a count would pass if the verb
rewrote an existing record in place.

8. NO LIVE WRITE. Consistent with T-401 and for the reason in T-400's section 6: the only live
runs were read-only plus one deliberate refusal. `attest.py trace` should still show three
acts on revision-doctrina and nothing else anywhere.
